From: Ethan Ramirez <ethan.ramirez@nimbus-sys.com>

Date: Fri, 14 Jun 2029 18:05:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal questions + outage impact

Rachel —

Thanks again for the conversation today. We’ve been reviewing the renewal and the infra incidents from last quarter; customer sentiment around reliability is the primary concern for our execs. To be candid, we are evaluating alternatives and need more comfort on two things before we proceed: a modest one-time economic concession to cover migration risk (they're asking ~25%) and a formal SLA top-up (response SLO and credits) for another 12 months.

Can Redwood do a limited co-funded bridge (credit applied to first invoice) and an SLA addendum that guarantees a shorter restore window for critical incidents? We don’t need long-term pricing changes — just a bridge to close the renewal with a timestamped SLA commitment.

Attaching our internal usage breakdown for context. Happy to jump on a call.

—Ethan
Nimbus Systems

Attachment: Nimbus_FY30_usage_breakdown.xlsx (xlsx)
From: rachel_kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Ethan Ramirez <ethan.ramirez@nimbus-sys.com>
Cc: nina.patel@nimbus-sys.com
Date: Fri, 14 Jun 2029 19:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal questions + outage impact

Ethan — thanks for the clear ask and the usage file. Appreciate the candor.

Short answer: we want to keep Nimbus as a reference-scale customer. I’ve outlined a proposal below we can put on the table immediately pending internal approval: 

- One-time bridge credit equal to 18% of the upcoming annual invoice, applied to the first month.
- SLA addendum: elevated P1 response window (30 min) and a capped incident credit that scales to 5% of monthly bill for eligible incidents, for 12 months.
- A 6-month term reset (move to 12-month commitment from renewal date) to help spread the impact.

I don’t have sign-off authority for above the 15% credit; I’ll escalate for Exec confirmation on the additional 3% and the SLA top-up. If that sounds directionally okay, I’ll pull in finance and ask for final approval today.

Can you confirm that 18% meets your internal ask for migration risk? If not, say so and I’ll escalate the delta.

Thanks —
Rachel Kim
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Folks — forwarding Nimbus thread. They are a strategic account (high-growth infra customer) and asking for: an 18% one-time bridge credit, an SLA addendum that tightens P1 response to 30m for 12 months, and a 6-month term reset.

What I can approve: up to 15% credit and standard SLA language. To get the full package we need exec sign-off for: 
1) Additional 3% one-time concession (total 18%)
2) The bespoke SLA top-up (shorter P1 window + expanded credits)
3) Approval to include a 6-month term reset on an annual commitment

Quick context: renewal ARR is ~$1.2M. The customer cited the March incident and risk of migration; finance has modeled that a partial credit + SLA addendum is cheaper than losing the account. I’ve attached a proposed credit schedule and a redline-ready SLA addendum for legal.

Asks: Vivek — can you green-light the extra 3% and confirm any commercial caveats?
David — need confirmation that the finance hit is acceptable and sign-off on contract language exposure.
Kimberly — legal needs to confirm we can commit to the specific response windows without further ops guarantees.

I’m available for a quick 20-min sync this morning if helpful.

Thanks,
Rachel

Team —

I agree to approve the additional 3% one-time bridge credit (bringing total to 18%) on a one-off basis, provided we treat this as a conditional retention concession tied to the following mandatory terms in the amendment: 

- Nimbus signs the 12-month SLA addendum with the specified P1 response SLA and credits.
- Term reset to 12 months and a non-cancelable 60-day window where pricing adjustments are locked.
- A joint post-mortem and quarterly reliability review for the first 6 months, executed by our Reliability team.

David — please confirm from finance that the modeled ROI still holds; if so, I’ll route final signature. Kimberly — please work with Legal to draft the addendum with clear cutoffs and a cap on total incident credits.
